To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mice deficient for the CCAAT/Enhancer binding protein β (C/EBPβ) develop an autoimmune disease similar to multicentric Castle man's disease (MCD) and that C/EBPB is essential for the correct function of the immune system.

the lack of C/EBPbeta leads to a lymphoproliferative phenotype with enhanced haemopoietis in the spleen, lymph nodes, liver and bone marrow, with an altered T helper response, and a strong susceptibility to C. albicans infection.
C/EBPB is required for the normal homeostatic control and function of haemopoieses, lymphocytes and macrophages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the immune and haemopoietictic response in the mouse, and with their potential application in human diseases.
the identification and characterization of genes and proteins involved in the regulation of haematopoiesis and immunity.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of Castleman's disease and with the elucidation of the role of C/EBP family members in the immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

C/EBPB is a key regulator of immune homeostasis, and the absence of this factor leads to a lymphoproliferative phenotype that is similar to that of mice overexpressing interleukin-2 and interleukin-3.
C/EBPB-deficiency leads to an imbalanced Th1/Th2 response, with a predominant Th2 phenotype, and that the lymphoproliferative disease in C/EBPB-/- mice is the consequence of this imbalance.
the absence of C/EBPbeta in mice is responsible for a severe deregulation of the immune system, with a strong bias towards the Th2 response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
C/EBPB is a key factor in the regulation of the IL- 6 gene expression, and that the lack of this factor leads to a severe lymphoproliferative disease with a T-helper imbalance.
C/EBB beta-deficient mice develop a pathology similar, if not identical, to Castleman's disease, and that this pathology is the result of an imbalanced T-helper function.

C/EBPB-deficient mice develop a lymphoproliferative syndrome with features similar to Castleman's disease and that the lymphoproliferation is associated with a strong imbalance between the T-helper 1 and T-helper 2 cytokine responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

C/EBPa is an important transcriptional activator of the IL-12p40 promoter, and that the absence of C/EBP alpha and C/EBP delta, which are also present in the IL-12 promoter, does not compensate for the lack of C/EBPa.
the absence of C/EBPbeta results in a severe deregulation of the immune system that leads to the development of lymphoproliferation and lymphoma.
C/EBPB is a crucial factor in the control of the immune response and that the loss of its function may lead to a lymphoproliferative disease.
